claims.value: Wales / Cape Prince of Wales, 17 Mar 2006

conflicts.assessment: Wales is supported by Karl's own diary; Nome in S21 is an error (Nome was where they met / Evergreen base).
Diary: left 17 Mar, landfall 31 Mar = 14 days (15 calendar days inclusive). Both counts consistent with same dates.

claims.value: reported themselves to Border Guard in Uelen

detained by border guards and moved to Lavrentiya

S1.title: Karl's journals – Central America (Panama, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Guatemala, Honduras)
S1.publisher: Goliath Expedition official website (goliath.mail2web.com), Wayback snapshot 2006-04-06
S1.quote: Wednesday, 4th April 2001. 8 degrees 51 minutes north, 79 degrees 49 minutes west. ... Within 45 minutes I had cleared the city and reached the America's Bridge, a huge construction spanning the Panama Canal. | Sunday, 20th May 2001 ... I reached the border ... It's then I find I have to pay $3 US to leave Costa Rica. | Thursday colour 30th August 2001. 14 degrees 21 minutes north, 92 degrees 10 minutes west. ... soon I'm within only 5k's of Mexico.

S2.title: Karl's journals – Mexico
S2.publisher: Goliath Expedition official website, Wayback snapshot 2006-10-21
S2.quote: Moving on, I quite quickly come to Tecun Uman ... From here I cross a fenced off bridge ... reaching a river which denotes the border. Crossing this bridge I finally arrive at a checkpoint in Mexico. ... I had to make a withdrawal from the 'hole in the wall' in the town of Hidalgo on the Mexican side. ... It's 37k's to Tapachula | ...slowly climbing up to rejoin the main road, Highway 15. | Tomorrow is the 'Coming in day' of 'Coming in days'! Nogales, this is it! The end of Latin America!

S3.title: Karl's journals – United States
S3.publisher: Goliath Expedition official website, Wayback snapshot 2008-10-06
S3.quote: Monday, 29th April 2002. US border, Nogales. ... I fill in my 'green card', pay my $6 and receive a 90 day visa waiver | Monday, 17th June 2002. Lake Havasu City. It's about 20 miles from here to the junction with Interstate Highway 40 | Last night I ended up close to the I-15, (Interstate 15). ... This is my only route north from here. | Tuesday, 31st December 2002. ... only 19 miles south of the Canadian border. I'm happy to find that on Exit 379 there's a small bar /cafe. | Thursday, 13th February 2003. ... Ruth drives everything back up to exit 379. After our goodbyes I am finally off, once again only 19 miles short of Canada. ... dropping down into Sweetgrass and the immigration crossing point.

S4.title: Karl's journals – Canada
S4.publisher: Goliath Expedition official website, Wayback snapshot 2006-04-14
S4.quote: Just over the border is the small town of Coutts. | I push on through the cold until I reach Medicine Hat | I'm throwing in a bit of a deviation to my route and making my way to the north- east, to the small town of Suffield. Here is BATUS | I will meet them at a truck stop near the small settlement of Bassano ... on 7th March. | Sunday, 9th March 2003. Dad hires a pick-up and we head off back to the truck stop where I'd been picked up. | The chapter ended with Karl's prolonged stay in Calgary as a number of people took the fight to the Immigration Service. | I leave Grande Prairie on 13th October and a couple of days later reach Beaverlodge. ... I head north-west about 100k's to Dawson Creek and the start of the Alaska Highway, arriving on the 22nd October. ... by the 25th reach Fort St John. | Thursday, 1st January 2004. Leaving Fort Nelson ... | Monday, 8th March 2004. I eventually arrive in Watson Lake | Saturday, 1st May 2004. I leave for the border ... I pass through Canadian Immigration just outside Beaver Creek

S5.title: Karl's journals – Alaska 2003-2005
S5.publisher: Goliath Expedition official website, Wayback snapshot 2006-04-06
S5.quote: Thursday, 13th May 2004. ... reach Dot Lake | Thursday, 16th December 2004. Having already walked to Murphy Dome I just need to have the sled brought up for me. ... a snow machine trail leaving the Dome ... drops onto the Minto Flats | Sunday, 10th January 2005. N 64 59.953' W 150 38.101' (Manley Hot Springs) | Thursday, 24th March 2005. ... DK plans to reach Unalakleet in one 36 mile push ... we entered the village at about 22:30. | My US visa is about to run out. ... I fly to Nome to pick up a flight to Fairbanks ... I shall go to Colombia.

S6.title: Karl's journals – Alaska 2005-2006
S6.publisher: Goliath Expedition official website, Wayback snapshot 2007-07-02
S6.quote: Extracts from Karl's diaries covering the Winter 2005 /06 from the point where Karl and Dimitri prepare in Fairbanks, Karl's move back to Unalakleet on the coast to complete his walk around to Cape Prince Wales and start of the crossing. He meets up again with Dimitri in Nome | Checking my GPS I find we are 28 miles out to sea, south-east of King Island!! | I'm dropped off 2 miles from Cape Douglas and the chopper leaves for Nome. ... I push on back up to the Cape | Tuesday, 21st February 2006. N65° 37.280' W168° 05.120' ... Wales, (population approximately 130) finally comes into view

S7.title: Extracts from Karl's diaries covering the Bering Straits Crossing 2006
S7.publisher: Goliath Expedition official website, Wayback snapshot 2007-06-29
S7.quote: Friday, 17th March 2006 Cape Prince of Wales ... We ease ourselves into the water after the sleds and begin to swim for the other side. ... Hundreds of metres wide | At this point we are drifting northwards at about 2mph | Monday, 20th March 2006 ... We are now in reverse and moving south at a similar speed. | we get to cross the Dateline and a 'nav check' puts us firmly in Russian waters. | We have been stuck at about 20 miles from the shore for three days now. | Today is also my 37th birthday ... only half a mile from landfall | Friday, 31st March 2006 ... It would appear we have come ashore right in the middle of the early-warning base about 3 miles north-west of Uelen ... The site is in fact abandoned. ... 'Terra firma - Terra firma.'

S8.title: Letter from Karl, 9th June 2006
S8.quote: There is not one yard between the town of Punto Arenas in Chile and Uelen in Russia that I have not walked or swam. There is no gap in the trail and that is my aim.

S13.title: Epic explorer crosses frozen sea
S13.quote: Karl Bushby reached land after 14 days walking across shifting plates of ice in temperatures reaching -30C. ... conquered the strait with temporary companion, Dimitri Kieffer, a French adventurer and specialist endurance racer. The pair had to take a roundabout 150-mile route to cross the 58-mile wide strait from Alaska to Siberia, crossing sheets of ice which were drifting with the current.

S16.title: Judge to decide explorer's fate
S16.quote: Karl Bushby, 36, from Hull, arrived near the unauthorised entry point of Uelen on 2 April having walked across the frozen Bering Strait from Alaska. He and fellow explorer Dimitri Kieffer were later detained by border guards and moved to the village of Lavrentiya.

S17.title: Explorer's world trek continues
S17.quote: A court in Russia's Far East has upheld an appeal by the British adventurer Karl Bushby against deportation. ... He must still pay a £40 fine, but will not now be expelled from Russia. Mr Bushby and fellow explorer American Dimitri Kieffer arrived near the unauthorised entry point of Uelen on 2 April. ... crossing from Alaska into Siberia via the frozen Arctic waters of the Chukchi Sea (north of the Bering Straits).

S25.title: Karl Bushby (Wikipedia, raw wikitext)
S25.quote: On 29 April 2002, Bushby left Mexico and entered the United States at Nogales, Arizona. Upon reaching Las Vegas in July, Bushby was told that his 90-day visa had expired and could not be renewed while he was in the United States. He thus flew back to Bogotá to apply for a six-month visa, returning to Las Vegas to resume the walk when his visa was approved in August. On New Year's Day 2003, a day away from crossing into Canada, Bushby's handcart was stolen while he was visiting a bar in Toole County, Montana. ... Between 17 and 31 March 2006, Bushby and French adventurer Dimitri Kieffer successfully crossed the Bering Strait on foot, having to take a roundabout 14-day route across a frozen 150-mile section to cross the 58-mile wide strait ... detained by Russian border troop officers while they were crossing the Russian border near the Chukotkan village of Uelen ... It was announced on 5 May 2006 that the Russian appeal court had upheld Bushby's application
